title: Dragon ewer
catalogueTitle: Ewer in the Shape of a Dragon
alt: Blue decoration covers a porcelain dragon with its mouth open and its tail curled up.
fact: The museum locates the filling hole in the tail and the outlet in the mouth.
limit: The location of the openings leaves the flow rate unmeasured.
front: Clip the inlet arrow to the tail and the outlet arrow to the mouth.
reverse: Park the timing strip beside the two opening marks.
frontResult: Two arrows sit on the copy. Each arrow has its own direction and its own opening.
reverseResult: The space for a flow rate stays empty. The two marked openings are still useful to the next reader.

title: Sawankhalok storage jar
dimensions: Diameter: 25.1 cm (9 7/8 in.); Overall: 33 cm (13 in.)
alt: A brown stoneware jar has a broad shoulder and a flared opening.
fact: The record gives a diameter of 25.1 cm and a separate overall measurement of 33 cm.
limit: The diameter entry leaves the width of the mouth unspecified.
front: Seat the diameter slip across the jar outline. Clip the overall slip separately.
reverse: Leave an open measure at the mouth.
frontResult: The slips sit in separate channels. A carrier can see which value means diameter.
reverseResult: The open space by the mouth tells the next carrier where to take another measurement.

title: Silk sampot
datedAs: Early twentieth-century dating in the catalogue.
alt: A long woven cloth has a dark patterned field and deep red ends.
fact: The record identifies silk in tabby weave with weft ikat and gives an overall measurement of 90.2 × 297.1 cm.
limit: The technique and extent leave the individual workshop unnamed.
front: Clip the silk and weave slips along the long cloth copy.
reverse: Slide an open-maker mark onto the cloth tag.
frontResult: The measured outline stays apart from the weave account. One label will travel with each edge.
reverseResult: The copy can travel with a named technique and an open line for the maker.

title: Bagobo shoulder basket
datedAs: The catalogue gives an approximate span.
context: Attributed to the Bagobo people in Davao, Philippines.
material: natural fibers, cloth, glass beads, metal
alt: A tall shoulder strap rises above a small basket with rows of bead decoration.
fact: The museum describes a rigid rattan basket covered with cotton, secured with abacá fibre stitching and decorated with glass beads.
limit: The structure leaves the identity of this basket’s owner open.
front: Pin rattan, cotton, abacá and beadwork to their separate callouts.
reverse: Lift the loose tab where the owner’s name would sit.
frontResult: The mounting strip now distinguishes the basket, cover, stitching and decoration.
reverseResult: That part of the record stays open. The Bagobo attribution still travels on the object label.

title: Pillow-end plate
alt: A patterned rectangular white-metal plate stands against a dark background.
fact: The plate has the component accession 1916.438.a. The catalogue marks the dimensional entry as an average.
limit: A value labelled as an average leaves the exact width of this component unconfirmed.
front: Set 1916.438.a under the single plate and place the average in its own channel.
reverse: Keep a blank space under this plate’s individual dimensions.
frontResult: Two slips sit side by side. The plate keeps its own reference number.
reverseResult: The exact size of this component will need its own record. The average stays readable in the other channel.

title: Glass box
alt: A small low glass box has a domed lid and gold-coloured decoration.
fact: The whole box has accession 1916.583. The museum catalogue also lists two component records.
limit: The linked accession numbers identify records. They leave the object’s individual owners unnamed.
front: Slide the two component pointers under the parent record.
reverse: Keep the ownership strip separate from the component links.
frontResult: The lookup now lets a clerk follow either component from the whole-box entry.
reverseResult: The component links stay useful. The ownership strip remains open for some other source.

title: Palembang shoulder cloth
material: weft ikat and gold, tabby weave, brocaded; silk and gold
alt: A red shoulder cloth has a patterned central field and wide bands at both ends.
fact: The museum records silk and gold, weft ikat, tabby weave and brocade.
limit: The image alone leaves the order of work in this maker’s workshop open.
front: Slide separate slips for the materials and the recorded techniques under the cloth view.
reverse: Lift the flap marked for an account of the working sequence.
frontResult: Silk and gold sit on the material line. The three construction descriptions travel on the second slip.
reverseResult: The copy can show the finished cloth while leaving room for a separate account of its making.

title: Kachchh skirt panel
datedAs: The catalogue retains both possible periods, late 1800s or early 1900s.
context: Attributed to Kachchh, Gujarat, western India.
alt: A red textile panel shows rows of embroidered circles above a dark green band.
fact: The museum records a panel of embroidered satin, with overall dimensions of 76.2 × 186.7 cm.
limit: A surviving panel leaves the finished garment’s full circumference open.
front: Hook the accession and size to the panel-shaped guide.
reverse: Leave the edge of the imagined garment on a translucent flap.
frontResult: The measured part and its accession travel together. A reader can follow the solid outline.
reverseResult: The flap lifts away easily. The panel measurement stays pinned to the photographed piece.

title: Jar with four ibex
datedAs: The date range is approximate. Quetta is qualified as probable.
context: Attributed to the Indus Valley civilization, probably Quetta, in present-day Pakistan.
alt: A wide low jar has dark animal designs alongside thin lines near its shoulder.
fact: The museum identifies four ibex in the decoration and gives the place attribution as probably Quetta.
limit: The four figures leave the maker’s working location unconfirmed.
front: Keep the four-figure count beside the decoration.
reverse: Slide the word probably beside Quetta on the place slip.
frontResult: The decoration count stays where a reader can compare it with the object.
reverseResult: A visitor can read the place attribution at its original strength. The count travels on the other slip.

title: Brisé fan
material: carved and pierced ivory sticks with three painted medallions in European style, held together by a white silk ribbon and an iron pin at the pivot point
dimensions: Radius: 21 cm (8 1/4 in.); Spread: 40.5 cm (15 15/16 in.)
alt: An open fan has pierced pale sticks and three round painted scenes.
fact: The museum gives a 21 cm radius and a spread of 40.5 cm. The record identifies a pivot pin and a ribbon.
limit: The open spread leaves the package dimensions of the closed fan unrecorded.
front: Rotate the radius guide to the pivot and clip the spread across the open fan.
reverse: Leave an empty span beside the folded profile.
frontResult: A carrier can follow the two measurements from different starting points.
reverseResult: A closed carrier would need a separate check. Its empty span remains visible beside the open position.

title: Joseon scroll box
catalogueTitle: Scroll Box with Dragon and Phoenix Design
datedAs: Century dating in the catalogue, attributed to the Joseon dynasty.
context: Attributed to Korea during the Joseon dynasty.
material: lacquered wood inlaid with mother-of-pearl and twisted brass and copper wire
alt: A long, narrow lidded box shows an intricate design in pale inlay.
fact: The museum gives an overall length of 87 cm and records lacquered wood with mother-of-pearl and metal wire.
limit: The overall measurement leaves the useful internal space unspecified.
front: Line the 87 cm slip up with the outside edge.
reverse: Lift a blank interior strip beside the exterior measurement.
frontResult: The known length stays on the outer edge of the case drawing.
reverseResult: A clerk will need another measurement before promising room for a scroll.

title: Ofuke kiln tea bowl
catalogueTitle: Tea bowl in the style of Vietnamese ware
institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art
datedAs: The museum dates this work to 1624–1641 in the Edo period.
context: Made at the Ofuke kiln in Nagoya, Aichi prefecture, Japan, according to the museum record.
material: Stoneware with white slip and cobalt decoration under clear glaze
alt: A pale footed stoneware bowl has a wide lip and faint blue decoration.
fact: The museum describes a Vietnamese style and records manufacture at the Ofuke kiln in Nagoya.
limit: The style description leaves the individual maker and the path of any exchanged design open.
front: Clip the Vietnamese-style slip and the Nagoya kiln slip to separate corners.
reverse: Leave the design’s route on the open leaf.
frontResult: Both slips can travel with the same accession. The place line remains Nagoya.
reverseResult: There is room for further sources on the design’s route. The museum’s two recorded descriptions stay visible.
